title: Prove the exact bounded-degree polynomial cost law and moments (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped counting proof with exact finite corroboration. This answers Open next question 1 of [PR4784](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4784): the exact cost law and closed moments for a uniformly chosen invertible two-role polynomial target of entry degree at most N over F_q[t]. The predecessor's joint exact-degree theorem is a cited premise, not an audit deliverable.

With minimum paid cost C, e=q^(-2N), and B(z)=q+q(q-1)z:

```text
E[z^C] = q^(-2N) [1+(q^2-1)z (B(z)^N-1)/(B(z)-1)]
E[C]   = (q-1)N/q + (1-e)/(q+1)
Var(C) = (q-1)N/q^2 + 2(q-1)Ne/[q(q+1)] - (1-e)(q-e)/(q+1)^2
```

The quotient denotes the finite geometric polynomial, including its removable value N at B=1. These formulas hold for every prime power q and N>=0, including the degree-zero free targets. At q=2,N=4 the mean is 597/256 and variance 51399/65536. The predecessor's existing binary target counts remain credited prior work; the new result is the closed law for this sampling measure.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit PR4784/4763/4276/4243, Wentao Li / PR4099 following PR2513, ToikY / PR4334, the retained local/semilocal lineage, and Nagao's classical polynomial-matrix presentation and degree method. The unchanged predecessor proof is the sole declared external mathematical input. Six files are added in `research/degree-bounded-polynomial-cost`.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19370254).

## Evidence

Before, PR4784 leaves bounded-degree moments open and supplies the exact-degree law. After, PROOF.md sums the correct finite mixture and derives the closed generating function, mean and variance, including the exceptional degree-zero terms.

- Complete polynomial coefficients and measured moments agree for all 495 integer pairs 2<=q<=16, 0<=N<=32. Non-prime-power q test arithmetic identities only.
- All 1,980 rational PGF evaluations pass, including every removable-pole case. A separate enumeration checks 7,362 weighted digit strings across 28 small mixtures. These are not new polynomial-matrix censuses.
- Three boundary fixtures and ten rejection controls pass. Explicit checks survive optimization. No predecessor scientific checker is imported or executed.
- Both warning-strict registered commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, timed at 0.091 s and 0.098 s. These are check durations, not a speed comparison. Normal and optimized generated hash-bound receipts are identical.
- Registered metadata/replay, syntax/JSON/function-size checks, committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export/input integrity pass at `6a5e7c58921a2efdeeb5ccdfcd1f1b0c528d1658`. Both modes pass from a read-only, Git-free export with empty PATH; all eight exported files retain their hashes. The worktree is clean.

From the repository root, using CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/degree-bounded-polynomial-cost/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/degree-bounded-polynomial-cost/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/degree-bounded-polynomial-cost
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/degree-bounded-polynomial-cost --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 executable may replace the local interpreter path. Expected markers are `PASS_DEGREE_BOUNDED_POLYNOMIAL_COST`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal result uses the cited PR4784 degree/cost theorem. Finite checks corroborate the new finite-sum formulas. Two roles, one-variable polynomial coefficients, base-field right vectors, free GL2(F_q) maps, invertible targets and uniform bounded-degree sampling are essential to the claim. Other measures, singular targets, other coefficient algebras and auxiliary roles are outside scope.

Native coefficient preparation, conversion, access, routing, control, precision, restoration, stock and complete supplier costs remain unpriced. No new kappa, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were outside scope and unrun. No external static analyzer is claimed; bounded managed allocation is documented.

## Open next questions

- Derive a quantitative normal-approximation error for this bounded-degree measure, starting with the geometric degree deficit and conditional binomial law. No uniform error estimate is supplied here.
- Identify an actual native polynomial-coefficient producer and consumer, and price coefficient preparation, conversion, restoration and the complete bill before applying these formal statistics to a supplier.

## Related open work

The completion refresh listed all fifteen account open PRs created since the advance CLAIM at 2026-11-03T09:10:26Z, including this PR, and checked the fourteen other titles and bodies for the polynomial target, degree-bounded sampling and PR4784 dependency. None studies this bounded-degree polynomial target-cost law or reports a competing value for it.

- [PR6560](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6560) minimizes fixed-involution reflection calls for a binary nilpotent chain. Its coefficient algebra and rank-one idempotent paid factors differ from this right-vector polynomial alphabet. No common target cost or sampling distribution is computed.

Merged PR4784 is the direct question source and mathematical dependency. Initial overlap covered 506 open PRs and 6,507 Discussion records with complete remote pagination, followed by a fresh latest-100 delta and live handoffs. Sparse local notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain limits. Canonical main was refreshed unchanged at `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priorities revision 8.
